raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan for my land.

---

I'm running 340 mu here in Quzhou — that's a real operation, not a small household plot. My dad and uncle helped me get started three years back, and I've been learning fast, but I still ask the old-timers and the extension guy when I'm not sure. With middle school education I can read the fertilizer bags and keep a simple account book, but I don't do fancy calculations like the university types.

Most of my land runs wheat-maize double crop — that's what works here, everyone does it. But I keep some fields separate for soybean and peanut because you can't plant maize on the same ground forever; the land gets tired and the bugs build up. My neighbor Old Zhang rotates soybeans in and he says it helps the maize the next year. Also, peanut prices have been decent the last two years, so I keep some in.

**Wheat (310 mu)** — I plant around October 10-15, right after the maize is off. I use improved varieties I buy from the seed company, not saved seed — the yield difference is worth the money. For fertilizer, I put a compound fertilizer down as base before plowing, then topdress urea at jointing in March when the wheat greens up. Last year I did about 18 kg N per mu total and got around 450 kg/mu, which I was happy with. I'll do similar this year. I irrigate before winter (December), at jointing, heading, and grain fill — that's four waterings. The well's pumping cost adds up but you can't skip them or yield drops fast.

**Maize (270 mu)** — Goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June, tight turnaround, usually 3-5 days. I hire a machine planter with fertilizer applicator; doing 270 mu by hand is impossible. Hybrid seed, about 18 kg N total split base and topdress. Irrigate once or twice if the summer rains don't come. Aiming for 500 kg/mu.

**Soybean (40 mu)** — Plant mid-June same window as maize, on fields that had maize for 2-3 years running. Less fertilizer since soybean fixes its own nitrogen. Honestly I'm still figuring soybean out — only my third year with it. Yields have been around 170-180 kg/mu.

**Peanut (30 mu)** — This is my "oilseed." Plant late April after spring warms up. Peanut needs more potassium and calcium, so I put down a special peanut compound. Irrigate 2-3 times. Good market price, especially if I can sell direct to the oil press in the county town.

I hire about 3 regular helpers through the season and more during wheat harvest and maize planting crunch. With 340 mu there's no way the four of us in the family can do it alone — I'd be crazy to try.

My main worry this year is diesel and fertilizer prices — both have been creeping up. If grain prices don't move, margins get thin. But I'm not changing my approach much from last year. Three years in, I've learned that big changes on a big farm can cost you real money if they don't work. I'll try new things on small patches first.
